Model a toy car: body is 200x100x100. Subtract 50x100x50 from a top front edge for the windshield. Add four 25-radius, 10-thick wheels aligned at the bottom corners, half embedded into body to form semicylindrical protrusions. | First, describe in words and step by step how the user's request can be implemented using function calls only. After the description, I will ask you to prepare the function call for execution, but don't execute it until I explicitly request it.

Implementation concept – step by step, using nothing but the provided functions

1  Define a reference system  
• Place the body’s rear-left-bottom corner at the global origin (0, 0, 0).  
• X-axis points forward, Y-axis points to the right, Z-axis points upward.  
  – Body therefore spans 0 → 200 mm in X, 0 → 100 mm in Y, 0 → 100 mm in Z.

2  Create the basic car body (initial solid) – one rectangular block  
• Call block() once with a single entry:  
  x_size = [200], y_size = [100], z_size = [100]  
  x = [0], y = [0], z = [0]                 (base corner at the origin)  
  subtraction = [False]                     (first block establishes the volume)

3  Carve the windshield cut-out – subtractive block  
• Windshield size: 50 × 100 × 50 (X × Y × Z).  
• It starts at the front-top edge: base point (150, 0, 50) – i.e.  
  – X = 200 − 50 = 150 (frontmost 50 mm)  
  – Y = 0 (entire width)  
  – Z = 50 (upper half of the 100 mm height)  
• Second call to block() with:  
  x_size = [50], y_size = [100], z_size = [50]  
  x = [150], y = [0], z = [50]  
  subtraction = [True]                      (this cuts the windshield void)

4  Add the four wheels – cylinders lying along the Y-axis  
Geometry interpretation  
• Wheel radius = 25; thickness (length along Y) = 10.  
• Half-embedded means the central plane of each wheel lies flush with the body side:  
  – Left side plane is Y = 0 → cylinder spans Y = −5 … 5 → baseCenterY = −5, heightVectY = 10.  
  – Right side plane is Y = 100 → spans 95 … 105 → baseCenterY = 95.  
• Vertical placement: center Z = radius = 25 so the bottom touches Z = 0.  
• Longitudinal placement:  
  – Rear wheels center at X = 25.  
  – Front wheels center at X = 175.  

Single cylinder() call with four entries (arrays):  
  baseCenterX = [25, 175, 25, 175]  
  baseCenterY = [-5, -5, 95, 95]  
  baseCenterZ = [25, 25, 25, 25]  
  heightVectX = [0, 0, 0, 0]  
  heightVectY = [10, 10, 10, 10]  
  heightVectZ = [0, 0, 0, 0]  
  radius = [25, 25, 25, 25]  
  subtraction = [False, False, False, False]        (wheels added)  
  cylinder_func = [0, 0, 0, 0]

5  Finish the model  
• Optionally call finished(allFunctionsCalled = True) to indicate no more geometry steps follow.

These five logical steps—two block() calls, one cylinder() call, and a concluding finished()—fully create the toy-car geometry exactly as specified, with every solid correctly positioned and topologically connected.
